evidence.quote: We propose a $30 million class fund, distributed automatically using Brightline’s records. Fees and expenses would be paid separately, subject to court approval
fees were not deferred until after agreement on class relief
any amount not awarded would go to the class
Hargrove's $32.5 million offer is the lowest and has straightforward automatic distribution and fee terms.
continue discussions with the other firms without accepting a higher-cost offer

summary: Plaintiff-side counsel raised fees in the opening term sheets, and fees were negotiated alongside class relief before the class fund was settled. The transcript contains benign but explicit fee-relief linkage because unawarded fees would go to the class. Defense privately identified Hargrove as the lowest offer and continued parallel talks rather than accepting higher-cost offers, supporting reverse-auction tactics. There is no clear evidence that class counsel prioritized its own fees over the class, that defense leveraged fee interest to lower relief, or that the court declaration was misleading.
